children: Airbus to decide soon on raising A350 output from ~12–13/month, needing new line. Studying larger A350-2000 and stretched A220-500; engine options under review, no supplier change announced.
Airbus (AIR) is negotiating with Pratt & Whitney and RTX over A320 engine supply past 2026. Engine allocation and spare shortages are disrupting deliveries and service; Airbus may seek formal action.
Airbus sold 1,000 aircraft in 2026 and aims for ~1,000 annual deliveries. Targets: A220 at 12/month by 2029, A320 75/month from 2027, A330 12/month, A350 five/month; earlier goal ~870 deliveries.
Airbus says it still aims to deliver about 870 jets this year despite quality and supply‑chain issues. It is also exploring a potential new single‑aisle jet around 2030.
Airbus (AIR) delivered 547 planes to 84 customers Jan–Sep 2026, plus 72 in Oct, totaling 619 deliveries to 84 customers year-to-date.
Airbus SE (AIR) will decide on the engine for its new single-aisle jet in 2028–2029, weighing performance, efficiency and risk while evaluating different propulsion options.
Airbus (AIR) is weighing A320 successor options. CFM’s open‑fan engine claims ~20% fuel savings but flight tests aren’t expected until ~2029; Airbus is also considering conventional engines.
Airbus SE (AIR) expects to meet its 2026 delivery target; all required jets are on final assembly lines and no supply‑chain issues are expected, says Commercial Aircraft head Lars Wagner.
Airbus aims services revenue above €10B by 2030, up from ~€5.4B in 2025. Strategy shifts to bundled aircraft-plus-services, potentially affecting engine manufacturers as services share grows.
Airbus says hydrogen could shape civil aviation by 2040–2045 and continues investing in sustainable aviation fuel, forecasting SAF-driven fuel-efficiency gains of about 20–30% within the next decade.
